laws.title: Bank Fraud and Capital Flight
laws.subtitle: Illegally transferring funds abroad during financial crisis
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon severe financial crisis has led to strict controls on capital transfers. Deliberately circumventing banking controls to illegally transfer funds abroad — particularly by bank insiders who enabled selective transfers — constitutes criminal bank fraud under Lebanese law.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; confiscation of transferred funds
exceptions: Legitimate authorized transfers under Central Bank regulations
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Banking Secrecy and Financial Regulation Laws

quiz.q: Why did Lebanon impose strict capital controls after 2019?
options: Due to a severe financial crisis threatening the banking system
quiz.explanation: Lebanon implemented capital controls due to a catastrophic financial crisis that threatened to collapse the entire banking system.

laws.title: Illegal Weapons Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning unauthorized firearms outside official militias
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits civilian possession of military-grade weapons, explosives, and unregistered firearms. Despite widespread illegal weapons in practice, the law criminalizes unauthorized possession. This is complicated by the presence of Hezbollah and other armed factions.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; forfeiture of weapons
exceptions: Licensed security companies
Hunters with valid permits
Military and police forces

quiz.q: What complicates Lebanon firearms law in practice?
options: The presence of multiple armed factions operating outside state control
quiz.explanation: Lebanon firearms law is complicated by the presence of Hezbollah and other armed factions operating outside the state monopoly on force.

laws.title: Drug Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Importing, selling, or distributing narcotics
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law criminalizes the trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The Bekaa Valley has historically been associated with drug cultivation, and Lebanon is a transit point for regional drug trafficking. Enforcement has been inconsistent but laws are severe.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment for large-scale trafficking; death penalty formerly applicable
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical production and distribution

quiz.q: What agricultural region of Lebanon has historically been associated with drug cultivation?
quiz.explanation: The Bekaa Valley has historically been associated with cannabis and other drug cultivation, making drug trafficking laws particularly relevant there.

laws.title: Public Fund Embezzlement
laws.subtitle: Misappropriating state funds by officials
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits embezzlement of public funds by government officials and civil servants. Given Lebanon chronic corruption challenges, this law is frequently cited but enforcement has historically been weak. Recent calls for accountability have increased attention to such cases.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment; full restitution; removal from office
exceptions: None — embezzlement of public funds is always criminal

quiz.q: What challenge has Lebanon historically faced in enforcing public embezzlement laws?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon has historically faced significant challenges enforcing embezzlement laws due to endemic corruption and political protection of officials.

laws.title: Human Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Exploiting people for labor or sexual purposes
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits all forms of human trafficking, including the exploitation of migrant domestic workers — a particularly serious problem given the kafala sponsorship system that creates conditions of vulnerability for workers from Ethiopia, Philippines, Sri Lanka, and other countries.
laws.penalty: 3 to 7 years imprisonment; financial penalties
exceptions: None — trafficking in any form is criminal

quiz.q: What labor system has made migrant domestic workers particularly vulnerable to trafficking in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: The kafala (sponsorship) system ties migrant workers to their employers, limiting their freedom and creating conditions of vulnerability to exploitation.

laws.title: Illegal Waste Dumping
laws.subtitle: Disposing of waste in unauthorized locations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon has faced severe waste management crises, most famously in 2015. Lebanese law prohibits dumping waste in unauthorized locations, including roadsides, rivers, and the Mediterranean coast. However, infrastructure limitations have made enforcement difficult.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for large-scale or toxic waste dumping
exceptions: None — proper waste disposal in licensed facilities is required

quiz.q: What major crisis highlighted Lebanon waste management failures?
quiz.explanation: The 2015 garbage crisis, when Beirut streets overflowed with uncollected trash, dramatically highlighted Lebanon waste management failures.

laws.title: Terrorism and Armed Group Membership
laws.subtitle: Participating in designated terrorist organizations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits membership in designated terrorist organizations and participation in terrorist acts. This is politically complex in Lebanon given that Hezbollah has both a political wing represented in parliament and a military wing. International terrorist designations differ from Lebanese domestic law.
laws.penalty: Hard labor; life imprisonment for leadership roles
exceptions: None for participation in recognized terrorist acts

quiz.q: Why is terrorism law application particularly complex in Lebanon?
options: Hezbollah is both in government and designated a terrorist group internationally
Lebanon relies only on military courts
quiz.explanation: Hezbollah participation in Lebanese government while being designated a terrorist organization internationally creates complex legal tensions.

laws.title: Defamation of the State and Public Officials
laws.subtitle: Publishing false statements damaging state reputation
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law includes strong defamation protections for the state, its symbols, and public officials. Criticizing government policy is permitted, but publishing deliberately false statements damaging to officials or state institutions can constitute criminal defamation.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: True statements
Good-faith criticism and opinion on public matters

quiz.q: Is criticism of government policy criminal under Lebanese defamation law?
options: No — criticism of policy is protected; false facts are not
Only if the official is named
quiz.explanation: Lebanese defamation law protects good-faith criticism of government policy while prohibiting deliberately false statements about officials.

laws.title: Drunk Driving
laws.subtitle: Operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese traffic law prohibits driving with a blood alcohol content exceeding the legal limit. Given the high rate of road accidents in Lebanon — among the highest in the region — drunk driving enforcement has increased in recent years.
laws.penalty: Fine; license suspension; imprisonment for repeat offenders or accidents caused
exceptions: None — any BAC above the limit is illegal while driving

quiz.q: How does Lebanon road accident rate compare regionally?
options: One of the lowest in the region
Among the highest in the region
quiz.explanation: Lebanon has one of the highest road accident rates in the region, making drunk driving enforcement a public safety priority.

laws.title: Arson
laws.subtitle: Deliberately setting fire to property or buildings
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law criminalizes deliberate arson — the intentional setting of fire to buildings, vehicles, agricultural land, or other property. Forest fires set deliberately are treated especially seriously given Lebanon forests vulnerable environmental state.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment; enhanced if people are harmed
exceptions: Controlled burns on own agricultural land with municipal permission
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against Property

quiz.q: Why are deliberately set forest fires treated especially seriously in Lebanon?
options: Lebanon forests are vulnerable and hard to restore
quiz.explanation: Lebanon forests are ecologically vulnerable and take decades to restore after fire, making deliberate arson particularly damaging and seriously treated.

laws.title: Illegal Antiquities Trade
laws.subtitle: Buying, selling, or exporting Lebanese archaeological artifacts
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon has an extraordinarily rich archaeological heritage spanning Phoenician, Roman, Ottoman, and other civilizations. Looting and trading in unregistered archaeological artifacts, or exporting them without authorization, is a serious violation of cultural heritage law.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; mandatory restitution
exceptions: Licensed antiquities dealers with properly registered pre-law collections

quiz.q: What civilizations contributed to Lebanon extraordinary archaeological heritage?
options: Phoenician, Roman, Ottoman, and other civilizations
quiz.explanation: Lebanon rich archaeological heritage spans Phoenician, Roman, Byzantine, Crusader, Ottoman, and other civilizations across millennia.

laws.title: Illegal Construction on Agricultural Land
laws.subtitle: Building on protected farmland without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law restricts construction on agricultural land to protect food production capacity and rural character. Unauthorized building on agricultural zones violates planning law and has contributed to the chaotic sprawl of Lebanese urban areas.
laws.penalty: Fine; demolition order; up to 2 years imprisonment for repeat violations
exceptions: Agricultural structures directly serving farm operations with planning permission

quiz.q: What urban challenge has unauthorized construction on agricultural land contributed to in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Unauthorized construction on agricultural land has contributed to Lebanon chaotic urban sprawl, consuming farmland and degrading landscape quality.

laws.title: Illegal Online Gambling
laws.subtitle: Operating or using unlicensed gambling platforms
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law restricts gambling to licensed establishments, primarily the Casino du Liban. Online gambling platforms not properly licensed under Lebanese law are illegal, and operating or promoting them targets Lebanese residents illegally.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment for operators
exceptions: Licensed Casino du Liban online operations if authorized

quiz.q: What is the main licensed gambling establishment in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Casino du Liban is the primary licensed gambling establishment in Lebanon, with a long history near Jounieh north of Beirut.

laws.title: Exploitation of Migrant Domestic Workers
laws.subtitle: Abusing or underpaying domestic workers under kafala
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese labor law protects workers from exploitation, but migrant domestic workers face special vulnerabilities under the kafala system. Withholding wages, confiscating passports, preventing workers from leaving, or subjecting them to physical abuse constitutes serious violations.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; possible deportation of employer nationals
exceptions: None — abuse of workers is always illegal
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Labor Act — Domestic Workers Provisions

quiz.q: What document is frequently illegally confiscated from migrant workers in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Passport confiscation is a common form of exploitation of migrant domestic workers in Lebanon, trapping them in their employment situation.

laws.title: Assassination and Political Violence
laws.subtitle: Killing or attempting to kill for political purposes
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon has a tragic history of political assassinations, including the killing of former Prime Minister Rafiq Hariri in 2005. Lebanese law criminalizes assassination and political violence, which the Special Tribunal for Lebanon also investigated under international law.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment; death penalty still formally on statute
exceptions: None — political violence is never legally justified

quiz.q: Which high-profile assassination in 2005 led to the establishment of the Special Tribunal for Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: The 2005 assassination of former Prime Minister Rafiq Hariri led to the establishment of the UN-backed Special Tribunal for Lebanon.

laws.title: Unlicensed Pharmaceutical Sales
laws.subtitle: Selling medicines without a pharmacy license
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law requires that pharmaceutical products be sold only through licensed pharmacies by qualified pharmacists. Selling medicines without a license, or dispensing prescription drugs without valid prescriptions, undermines patient safety.
laws.penalty: Fine; pharmacy license revocation; up to 2 years imprisonment
exceptions: Emergency dispensing in genuine life-threatening situations
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Pharmaceuticals and Drug Control Act

quiz.q: Who may legally dispense pharmaceutical products in Lebanon?
options: Anyone with basic first aid training
quiz.explanation: Only licensed pharmacists operating in licensed pharmacies may legally dispense pharmaceutical products in Lebanon.

laws.title: Commercial Fraud
laws.subtitle: Deceiving business partners for financial gain
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese commercial law prohibits deliberate deception in business transactions, including misrepresenting goods, false invoicing, and fraudulent contract performance. The fragile Lebanese economy makes commercial fraud especially damaging to business trust.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Good-faith commercial disputes and honest mistakes
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Code of Commerce — Fraud Provisions

quiz.q: How does Lebanon economic situation affect the impact of commercial fraud?
options: The fragile economy makes fraud especially damaging to business trust
Economic crisis means fraud is more tolerated
Fraud is more profitable in a weak economy
quiz.explanation: Lebanon already fragile economy makes commercial fraud particularly damaging, as it further erodes the business trust needed for economic recovery.

laws.title: Sectarian Incitement
laws.subtitle: Promoting violence or hatred between religious communities
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon confessional political system divides power among 18 recognized religious communities. Deliberately inciting sectarian hatred, violence, or discrimination between these communities is a serious criminal offense that threatens Lebanon delicate social fabric.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment; enhanced if violence results
exceptions: Academic analysis of sectarian issues
Religious leaders theology within their communities

quiz.q: How many recognized religious communities does Lebanon confessional system divide power among?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon power-sharing system recognizes 18 religious communities, making laws against sectarian incitement vital for maintaining social peace.

laws.title: Cybercrime and Online Fraud
laws.subtitle: Committing fraud or accessing systems illegally online
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon Cybercrime Law criminalizes unauthorized access to computer systems, online fraud, phishing, and interception of electronic communications. As digital banking and commerce have grown, cybercrime enforcement has become more active.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment; up to 7 years for financial cybercrime
exceptions: Authorized security testing by certified professionals

quiz.q: When was Lebanon Cybercrime Law enacted?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon enacted its Cybercrime Law in 2018, updating the legal framework to address modern digital offenses including online fraud and unauthorized access.

laws.title: Money Laundering
laws.subtitle: Concealing proceeds of criminal activity
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits money laundering — converting proceeds of criminal activity into seemingly legitimate assets. Lebanon financial system, known for banking secrecy, has faced international pressure to strengthen AML enforcement. The Special Investigation Commission oversees suspicious transactions.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; confiscation of laundered assets
exceptions: None — knowing participation in money laundering is criminal

quiz.q: What oversight body handles suspicious transaction reports in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon Special Investigation Commission receives and investigates suspicious transaction reports from financial institutions to combat money laundering.

laws.title: Mediterranean Sea Pollution
laws.subtitle: Dumping waste or pollutants into the Mediterranean
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon Mediterranean coastline is environmentally sensitive and culturally important. Dumping sewage, industrial waste, or other pollutants into the sea violates environmental law and international agreements. Lebanon faces significant challenges with untreated sewage flowing into the sea.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for deliberate industrial dumping
exceptions: Emergency release with immediate reporting and remediation
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Environmental Protection Act — Marine Pollution

quiz.q: What is one of Lebanon most significant Mediterranean pollution problems?
options: Untreated sewage flowing into the sea
quiz.explanation: Untreated sewage flowing directly into the Mediterranean is one of Lebanon most significant marine pollution challenges.

laws.title: Counterfeiting Currency
laws.subtitle: Producing or distributing fake Lebanese pounds or foreign currency
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits the production, distribution, or use of counterfeit currency. Given Lebanon ongoing currency crisis and the circulation of both Lebanese pounds and US dollars, currency fraud takes on additional significance.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years
exceptions: Clearly marked replicas for artistic or educational purposes not passable as genuine currency

quiz.q: Which two currencies commonly circulate in Lebanon increasing currency fraud complexity?
quiz.explanation: Both Lebanese pounds and US dollars circulate in Lebanon economy, making currency counterfeiting particularly complex to monitor.

laws.title: Child Marriage
laws.subtitle: Marrying children under the minimum legal age
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon lacks a unified civil personal status code, with marriage laws governed by 15 different religious courts for different communities. Some religious court systems set very low minimum ages. Civil society has long called for reform, but a unified civil code has not been enacted.
laws.penalty: Varies by religious court jurisdiction; civil and criminal liability possible
exceptions: Varies by confessional community — significant variation remains

quiz.q: How many different religious court systems govern personal status matters including marriage in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon has 15 different religious court systems governing personal status matters, including marriage age requirements, for different communities.

laws.title: Illegal Drug Manufacturing
laws.subtitle: Producing controlled substances without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits unauthorized production of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. While Bekaa Valley cannabis cultivation has historical roots, production of synthetic drugs or refining of opiates without licensing constitutes a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for 10 to 20 years
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical manufacturers under health ministry oversight

quiz.q: What crop has historically been cultivated in Lebanon Bekaa Valley region?
quiz.explanation: Cannabis cultivation has historical roots in Lebanon Bekaa Valley, making drug manufacturing law particularly relevant in that region.

laws.title: Burglary
laws.subtitle: Breaking into property to steal
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law punishes the unlawful entry into homes, businesses, or other premises with intent to steal or commit other crimes. Breaking and entering with criminal intent carries significantly enhanced penalties compared to ordinary theft.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 7 years; up to 10 years for aggravated burglary
exceptions: None for intentional breaking and entering with criminal intent

quiz.q: What element distinguishes burglary from simple theft in Lebanese law?
options: Use of a vehicle for escape
quiz.explanation: Burglary in Lebanon is distinguished by unlawful entry into premises, which adds significant criminal weight to the underlying theft offense.

laws.title: Assault Causing Grievous Bodily Harm
laws.subtitle: Attacking someone causing serious physical injury
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese penal law punishes physical attacks that cause serious bodily injury — broken bones, disfigurement, disability, or long-term health damage. Such assaults are treated as serious violent crimes regardless of the relationship between attacker and victim.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; enhanced if premeditated or against a family member
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense
Medical procedures with consent

quiz.q: What factor increases assault penalties under Lebanese law?
quiz.explanation: Premeditated assault causing grievous bodily harm carries enhanced penalties under Lebanese law compared to assault committed in the heat of the moment.

laws.title: Domestic Violence
laws.subtitle: Physical or psychological abuse of family members
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon enacted Law 293 in 2014 to combat domestic violence, the first such law in the Arab world. It criminalizes physical violence within the family and provides for protection orders. However, the law was criticized for not criminalizing marital rape.
laws.penalty: Up to 1 year imprisonment; enhanced for repeat offenses; protection orders available
exceptions: None for physical violence within the family
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Law 293 on Protection of Women and Family Members (2014)

quiz.q: What was significant about Lebanon Law 293 of 2014?
options: It was the first law to criminalize divorce
It was the first domestic violence law in the Arab world
quiz.explanation: Lebanon Law 293 of 2014 was the first law criminalizing domestic violence in the Arab world, a landmark even though criticized for its limitations.

laws.title: Genocide and War Crimes
laws.subtitle: Mass atrocities and violations of humanitarian law
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon criminal law incorporates international crimes including genocide and war crimes. Lebanon civil war (1975–1990) and subsequent conflicts have made these provisions particularly significant. Lebanon has cooperated with international tribunals on accountability.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment; hard labor
exceptions: None — atrocity crimes admit no legal justification

quiz.q: What period defined Lebanon experience with civil war and atrocity crimes?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon civil war from 1975 to 1990 was a period of devastating conflict involving numerous factions and documented atrocities.

laws.title: Securities and Investment Fraud
laws.subtitle: Defrauding investors through misrepresentation
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits fraudulent investment schemes and misrepresentation in securities markets. The Capital Markets Authority oversees securities regulation. Investment fraud has been a significant concern in the context of Lebanon financial crisis.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Good-faith investment projections that prove wrong due to unforeseen circumstances

quiz.q: Which body regulates securities markets in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon Capital Markets Authority oversees securities regulation and investor protection in the country financial markets.

laws.title: Unlawful Possession of Military Explosives
laws.subtitle: Owning military-grade explosives without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law strictly prohibits civilian possession of military explosives, detonators, and related materials. The catastrophic 2020 Beirut port explosion — caused by improperly stored ammonium nitrate — highlighted the deadly consequences of explosive material mismanagement.
laws.penalty: Hard labor; up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed demolition and mining companies with proper permits

quiz.q: What catastrophic event highlighted the dangers of explosive material mismanagement in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: The devastating 2020 Beirut port explosion, caused by improperly stored ammonium nitrate, killed over 200 people and highlighted explosive storage dangers.

laws.title: Forgery of Official Documents
laws.subtitle: Creating or using falsified government documents
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits the forgery of official documents including identity cards, passports, academic certificates, and legal contracts. Document forgery undermines the integrity of official systems and enables other crimes.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 3 years; enhanced if used to commit other crimes
exceptions: Theatrical props clearly not passable as genuine documents

quiz.q: What types of documents are most commonly forged in Lebanon according to law enforcement?
options: Identity cards, passports, and academic certificates
quiz.explanation: Identity cards, passports, and academic certificates are among the most commonly forged official documents targeted by Lebanese forgery laws.

laws.title: Kidnapping
laws.subtitle: Abducting a person by force or coercion
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon has experienced kidnappings for ransom and political purposes, particularly during the civil war era and regional instability. Lebanese law treats kidnapping as a serious violent crime with severe penalties, especially when victims are harmed or ransom demanded.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years; life imprisonment if victim killed
exceptions: None — kidnapping in any form is serious criminal offense
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against Freedom

quiz.q: During what period did Lebanon experience the highest rates of politically motivated kidnappings?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon civil war era (1975-1990) saw numerous politically motivated kidnappings of Lebanese citizens and foreign nationals.

laws.title: Obstruction of Justice
laws.subtitle: Interfering with legal proceedings or investigations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits obstructing police investigations and judicial proceedings. This includes witness intimidation, evidence tampering, and bribing officials. Given Lebanon challenges with political interference in justice, this law is particularly significant.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate legal defense within ethical professional rules

quiz.q: What challenges make obstruction of justice laws especially significant in Lebanon?
options: Lebanon has very few criminal cases
Political interference in the justice system
quiz.explanation: Lebanon has faced significant challenges with political interference in judicial proceedings, making obstruction of justice laws particularly important.

laws.title: Smoking in Prohibited Spaces
laws.subtitle: Smoking in enclosed public spaces and workplaces
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese Law 174 prohibits smoking in all enclosed public spaces including restaurants, cafes, offices, and government buildings. Despite widespread smoking culture in Lebanon, this law was passed to protect non-smokers from secondhand smoke.
laws.penalty: Fine of 200,000 LBP for individuals; larger fines for business owners
exceptions: Designated outdoor smoking areas meeting separation requirements

quiz.q: What was the purpose of Lebanese Law 174?
options: To prohibit smoking in enclosed public spaces
quiz.explanation: Lebanese Law 174 prohibits smoking in enclosed public spaces to protect non-smokers from the health risks of secondhand smoke.

laws.title: Credit and Banking Fraud
laws.subtitle: Fraudulently obtaining credit or misusing banking services
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese banking law prohibits obtaining credit through false representations, misusing credit facilities, and bouncing checks intentionally. Given Lebanon banking crisis, fraudulent exploitation of banking services has become an acute concern.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; checkbook cancellation
exceptions: Genuine financial difficulties with good-faith communication to bank

quiz.q: What document practice became a significant fraud issue in Lebanon banking context?
quiz.explanation: Intentionally bouncing checks — writing checks without sufficient funds to honor them — is a serious banking fraud offense in Lebanon.

laws.title: Treason and Collaboration with Enemy States
laws.subtitle: Assisting foreign enemies against Lebanon
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law criminalizes collaboration with enemy states or armed forces acting against Lebanon sovereignty. Given Lebanon complex geopolitical position — with Israel as a formal enemy state — collaboration with Israeli military or intelligence is treated as treason.
laws.penalty: Death penalty or hard labor for life
exceptions: None — treason is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against State Security

quiz.q: Which country does Lebanese law specifically treat as an enemy state due to historical conflict?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon and Israel remain in a formal state of war, making collaboration with Israeli military or intelligence forces an act of treason under Lebanese law.

laws.title: Torture by Public Officials
laws.subtitle: Subjecting detainees to cruel or inhumane treatment
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon ratified the UN Convention Against Torture and its law prohibits torture by public officials, including police and military personnel. Human rights organizations have documented torture in Lebanese detention facilities, highlighting the gap between law and practice.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years; up to life imprisonment if death results
exceptions: None — torture is absolutely prohibited

quiz.q: What international convention has Lebanon ratified regarding torture?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon has ratified the UN Convention Against Torture, committing to prohibit and prosecute torture by public officials.

laws.title: Illegal Gambling Operations
laws.subtitle: Running unlicensed gambling establishments
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law restricts gambling to licensed establishments. Running unlicensed gambling operations — including underground poker rooms, illegal sports betting operations, and unauthorized slot machine parlors — is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; equipment confiscation
exceptions: Casino du Liban and licensed establishments with valid permits

quiz.q: What is the legal status of underground gambling rooms in Lebanon?
options: Legal if no money is exchanged
quiz.explanation: Underground gambling operations are illegal in Lebanon regardless of scale. Only licensed establishments like Casino du Liban may operate legally.

laws.title: Forest Destruction
laws.subtitle: Illegally cutting or burning protected forests
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon cedar and pine forests are national symbols and ecologically vital. Cutting trees in protected forest areas or setting forest fires — whether deliberately or through negligence — is a serious environmental crime. Lebanon has lost much of its historic forest cover.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for deliberate forest destruction
exceptions: Licensed timber operations in non-protected areas under forestry management plans

quiz.q: What tree species is particularly symbolic of Lebanon and its national identity?
quiz.explanation: The cedar of Lebanon is the national symbol featured on the Lebanese flag, making forest protection deeply tied to national identity.

laws.title: Unlawful Detention
laws.subtitle: Illegally imprisoning or restricting a person freedom
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits the unlawful detention or confinement of individuals — holding people without legal authority, arresting without warrant when not permitted, or confining individuals against their will. This applies to both private individuals and public officials who exceed their authority.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; enhanced if detention is prolonged or cruel
exceptions: Lawful arrest with proper authority
Parental supervision of minor children
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against Freedom

quiz.q: Does the prohibition on unlawful detention in Lebanon apply to public officials who exceed their authority?
options: Yes — both officials and private persons are covered
Only to foreigners detaining Lebanese citizens
quiz.explanation: Lebanese law prohibiting unlawful detention applies both to private individuals and public officials who detain people beyond their legal authority.

laws.title: Human Organ Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Buying or selling human organs for transplantation
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits commercial trade in human organs. While Lebanon has a registered organ donation system, buying or selling kidneys, livers, or other organs is criminalized. The financial desperation from Lebanon economic crisis has increased vulnerability to organ trafficking.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years
exceptions: Voluntary, non-commercial organ donation between family members or altruistic donors

quiz.q: How has Lebanon economic crisis affected organ trafficking risks?
options: It has reduced trafficking by reducing demand
Financial desperation has increased vulnerability to exploitation
The crisis ended the medical system needed for transplants
quiz.explanation: Lebanon devastating economic crisis has increased the vulnerability of desperate citizens to organ traffickers who exploit financial need.

laws.title: Online Defamation and Cyberbullying
laws.subtitle: Harassing or defaming individuals through digital platforms
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon 2018 Cybercrime Law addresses online defamation, cyberbullying, and digital harassment. Publishing false and damaging statements about individuals online, or conducting systematic campaigns of online harassment, is criminalized.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: Factual criticism and opinion on public figures public conduct
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Cybercrime Law (2018) — Personal Dignity Provisions

quiz.q: When did Lebanon enact specific cybercrime legislation addressing online harassment?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon enacted the Cybercrime Law in 2018, which specifically addresses online defamation and cyberbullying in addition to other digital offenses.

laws.title: Illegal Fuel Import and Distribution
laws.subtitle: Smuggling or distributing fuel without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon fuel sector has been plagued by corruption, smuggling, and shortages, particularly during the economic crisis. Importing or distributing fuel without proper licensing, or smuggling subsidized fuel across borders, constitutes a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; seizure of fuel
exceptions: Licensed importers and distributors operating within regulated quotas

quiz.q: What exacerbated Lebanon fuel sector problems during the economic crisis?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon fuel sector problems were exacerbated by corruption, smuggling of subsidized fuel abroad, and abuse of the subsidy system during the economic crisis.

laws.title: Electricity Infrastructure Sabotage
laws.subtitle: Damaging power infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon electricity sector is chronically underpowered, with residents relying on private generator networks to supplement insufficient state supply. Deliberately sabotaging electricity infrastructure — generators, substations, or transmission lines — is a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; enhanced if people harmed
exceptions: None for intentional sabotage

quiz.q: What do Lebanese residents commonly rely on to supplement insufficient state electricity supply?
quiz.explanation: Private generator networks operated by neighborhood suppliers supplement the state electricity supply, which typically provides only a few hours per day.

laws.title: Port Corruption and Customs Fraud
laws.subtitle: Bribing port officials or falsifying import declarations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon ports, particularly Beirut Port, have been affected by systemic corruption. Bribing port officials to clear goods without inspection, falsifying import declarations, or using the port to smuggle contraband constitutes serious criminal offenses.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; confiscation of goods; fines equal to evaded duties
exceptions: Good-faith declaration errors with voluntary correction

quiz.q: What major disaster was partly linked to corruption and negligence at Beirut Port?
quiz.explanation: The 2020 Beirut port explosion was partly attributed to corruption and negligence in the handling and storage of hazardous materials at the port.

laws.title: Degree and Diploma Fraud
laws.subtitle: Using fraudulent academic credentials
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits using fraudulent academic degrees or diplomas to obtain employment, professional licenses, or other benefits. Academic credential fraud is particularly damaging in professional fields like medicine and engineering where qualifications directly affect public safety.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; dismissal from position obtained through fraud
exceptions: Honest errors in credential representation with prompt correction

quiz.q: Why is academic credential fraud especially dangerous in professional fields in Lebanon?
options: Unqualified professionals in medicine and engineering endanger public safety
It reduces competition for qualified graduates
quiz.explanation: In medicine and engineering, fraudulently obtained credentials allow unqualified people into roles where their incompetence can directly endanger lives.

laws.title: Illegal Possession of Military Weapons
laws.subtitle: Possessing rockets, artillery, or military-grade arms
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits civilian possession of military weapons including rockets, mortars, heavy machine guns, and artillery. The law has limited effectiveness given the presence of Hezbollah military infrastructure, but civilian possession outside factional control is criminalized.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years
exceptions: Official Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces
Authorized state security services
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Arms Regulation Act — Military Weapons

quiz.q: What limits the practical enforcement of Lebanon law on military weapons possession?
options: The law was only recently enacted
The presence of Hezbollah military infrastructure outside state control
Military weapons are not defined in law
quiz.explanation: Lebanon law on military weapons is practically limited by Hezbollah substantial military infrastructure operating outside Lebanese Armed Forces command.

laws.title: Illegal Wildlife Trade
laws.subtitle: Buying or selling protected animal species
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon is on major bird migration routes, and its wildlife includes protected species. Trading in protected birds, reptiles, and other wildlife — including as exotic pets — violates Lebanese environmental law and international conventions.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; confiscation of animals
exceptions: Licensed zoos and research facilities with proper permits

quiz.q: Why is Lebanon particularly important in terms of bird conservation?
options: It has the most bird species in the world
It sits on major bird migration routes
It is home to the rarest eagle species
quiz.explanation: Lebanon geographical position on major bird migration routes between Africa and Eurasia makes it particularly significant for bird conservation.

laws.title: Contempt of Court
laws.subtitle: Disrespecting or disobeying court orders
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law requires respect for the judiciary and compliance with court orders. Deliberately disobeying court orders, publicly insulting judges, or disrupting court proceedings constitutes contempt of court. Given Lebanon governance challenges, judicial respect is a priority.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; enhanced for organized contempt
exceptions: Good-faith appeals of court decisions through proper legal channels
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Code of Civil Procedure — Contempt Provisions

quiz.q: Which type of court behavior constitutes contempt in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Deliberately disobeying court orders constitutes contempt of court in Lebanon, carrying potential imprisonment.

laws.title: Espionage for Foreign Powers
laws.subtitle: Collecting state secrets for foreign intelligence agencies
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits the collection, storage, or transmission of state secrets to foreign governments or organizations. Given Lebanon complex geopolitical environment with multiple foreign intelligence operations active in the country, espionage prosecutions have been reported.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for life in extreme cases; up to 20 years for lesser espionage
exceptions: Authorized intelligence cooperation under bilateral agreements
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Espionage and State Security

quiz.q: What makes espionage prosecution complex in Lebanon geopolitical environment?
options: Multiple foreign intelligence operations are active in Lebanon
Lebanon has no bilateral defense agreements
quiz.explanation: Lebanon complex geopolitical position, with multiple foreign intelligence services active in the country, makes espionage cases particularly complex.

laws.title: Consumer Fraud and Price Gouging
laws.subtitle: Overcharging consumers especially during crises
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese consumer protection law prohibits price gouging and fraud against consumers, particularly during crisis situations. During Lebanon economic meltdown and COVID-19 pandemic, some merchants exploited shortages to charge excessive prices, triggering enforcement actions.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; business closure
exceptions: Legitimate price adjustments reflecting genuine supply costs

quiz.q: When did price gouging become a particularly acute enforcement issue in Lebanon?
options: During the economic crisis and COVID-19 pandemic
quiz.explanation: Lebanon economic collapse and COVID-19 pandemic created conditions where merchants exploited shortages to charge excessive prices, triggering enforcement of price gouging laws.

laws.title: Unauthorized Medical Procedures
laws.subtitle: Performing medical operations without proper licensing
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law requires that all medical procedures be performed by licensed healthcare professionals in authorized facilities. Performing unauthorized medical procedures — including illegal cosmetic operations, abortions outside legal frameworks, or other interventions — is criminalized.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if harm results
exceptions: Emergency procedures to preserve life in situations where no licensed provider is available

quiz.q: What type of unauthorized medical procedures has become particularly common in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Illegal cosmetic operations performed by unlicensed practitioners have become a significant concern in Lebanon, causing serious harm in some cases.

laws.title: Maritime Smuggling
laws.subtitle: Using the sea to smuggle contraband
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon extensive Mediterranean coastline provides opportunities for maritime smuggling of weapons, drugs, and migrants. Lebanese naval and coast guard authorities work to intercept smuggling operations. The porous maritime border has been exploited by various criminal and armed groups.
laws.penalty: Hard labor; up to 15 years depending on nature of contraband
exceptions: Legal shipping operations with proper manifests and customs clearance

quiz.q: What geographic feature makes maritime smuggling a particular challenge for Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon extensive Mediterranean coastline provides numerous points where smugglers can land contraband away from official border crossings.

laws.title: Real Estate Fraud
laws.subtitle: Deceiving buyers in property transactions
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese property law prohibits fraudulent real estate transactions including selling properties one does not own, concealing liens and encumbrances, and misrepresenting property conditions. Real estate fraud is particularly damaging given Lebanon housing market importance.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for organized real estate fraud
exceptions: Good-faith errors disclosed to buyers before transaction completion

quiz.q: What specific deception in real estate is prohibited under Lebanese law?
options: Advertising at higher than asking price
Concealing property liens and encumbrances from buyers
quiz.explanation: Concealing liens, mortgages, and other encumbrances on property from buyers is a form of real estate fraud prohibited under Lebanese law.

laws.title: Recruitment into Armed Groups
laws.subtitle: Recruiting civilians into non-state armed organizations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits recruiting civilians into armed groups outside the official Lebanese state forces. This applies to militia recruitment, foreign fighter recruitment, and any other effort to build non-state armed capacity. Enforcement is politically complex given Lebanon sectarian dynamics.
laws.penalty: Hard labor; up to 15 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Official Lebanese Armed Forces recruitment

quiz.q: What political complexity affects enforcement of armed group recruitment laws in Lebanon?
options: Lebanon sectarian political dynamics protect some armed groups
quiz.explanation: Lebanon complex sectarian politics means that some armed groups enjoy political protection, complicating enforcement of recruitment prohibition laws.

laws.title: Identity Theft
laws.subtitle: Using another person identity for fraudulent purposes
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits assuming another person identity for fraudulent purposes. Identity theft includes using stolen identity documents, creating fake online profiles to impersonate others, and using personal information obtained without consent for illegal purposes.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; enhanced if used to commit other crimes
exceptions: Parody and satire clearly not representing genuine identity theft
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Cybercrime Law (2018) and Penal Code

quiz.q: What law specifically addresses online identity theft in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon 2018 Cybercrime Law specifically addresses online identity theft and impersonation as digital offenses.

laws.title: Illegal Quarrying
laws.subtitle: Operating rock and mineral quarries without permits
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon mountains and hills have been extensively scarred by illegal quarrying for construction materials. Unauthorized quarrying destroys landscapes, destabilizes hillsides, creates flood risks, and contributes to environmental degradation. Enforcement has historically been inconsistent.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; mandatory site rehabilitation
exceptions: Licensed quarry operations meeting environmental and safety standards

quiz.q: What environmental damage has illegal quarrying caused to Lebanon landscape?
options: Scarred mountains, unstable hillsides, and increased flood risks
quiz.explanation: Illegal quarrying has scarred Lebanon mountains, destabilized hillsides, and increased flood and landslide risks across the country.

laws.title: Medical Malpractice
laws.subtitle: Professional negligence by healthcare providers
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law provides for both civil and criminal liability for medical malpractice. When medical negligence falls significantly below accepted standards of care and causes patient harm, healthcare providers may face criminal prosecution in addition to civil damages.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for criminal negligence; medical license suspension
exceptions: Acceptable complications occurring despite proper standard of care
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Medical Professions Law — Malpractice Provisions

quiz.q: What distinguishes criminal medical malpractice from a civil claim in Lebanon?
options: Criminal cases always result in imprisonment
Criminal malpractice requires gross negligence below accepted standards
Criminal cases are tried in military courts
quiz.explanation: Criminal medical malpractice in Lebanon requires negligence that falls significantly below accepted standards of care, not merely a poor outcome.

laws.title: Fuel Hoarding During Shortages
laws.subtitle: Stockpiling subsidized fuel for resale at higher prices
laws.fullDescription: During Lebanon fuel crisis, hoarding of subsidized fuel — particularly diesel for generators — to resell at black market prices became widespread. Lebanese law prohibits hoarding of essential commodities to create artificial shortages and profit from price manipulation.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; confiscation of hoarded fuel
exceptions: Normal household fuel storage within reasonable limits
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Internal Trade Act — Essential Commodities

quiz.q: Why was fuel hoarding particularly damaging during Lebanon crisis?
options: It created artificial shortages of essential generator fuel
It only affected the wealthiest consumers
quiz.explanation: Fuel hoarding created artificial shortages of diesel needed for private generators that Lebanese rely on when state electricity fails, affecting everyone.

laws.title: Murder
laws.subtitle: Unlawful intentional killing of another person
laws.fullDescription: Murder is the most serious crime under Lebanese law. The deliberate, premeditated killing of another person carries the most severe penalties available in the Lebanese penal system. Aggravating circumstances — premeditation, use of poison, multiple victims — increase the penalty.
laws.penalty: Death penalty or hard labor for life
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense
Accidental death without criminal negligence
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against Life

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for premeditated murder under Lebanese law?
options: Death penalty or hard labor for life
quiz.explanation: Premeditated murder in Lebanon carries the death penalty or hard labor for life — the most severe penalties available under Lebanese law.

laws.title: Cannabis Cultivation for Export
laws.subtitle: Growing cannabis intended for drug trafficking
laws.fullDescription: While small-scale cannabis cultivation has historical roots in Lebanon Bekaa Valley, cultivating cannabis for export as part of drug trafficking networks is a serious criminal offense. International drug trafficking organizations have exploited Lebanon agricultural conditions.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for 10 to 20 years for trafficking cultivation
exceptions: No commercial exception — all unauthorized cultivation for export is criminal

quiz.q: What geographical feature makes Lebanon Bekaa Valley attractive for drug cultivation?
options: Fertile soil and favorable growing conditions
quiz.explanation: The Bekaa Valley fertile soil and Mediterranean climate create favorable agricultural conditions that have historically been exploited for cannabis cultivation.

laws.title: Illegal Eviction of Tenants
laws.subtitle: Forcibly removing tenants without legal process
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese tenancy law provides strong protections for long-term tenants, especially under older rent control laws. Forcibly evicting tenants without going through proper legal procedures — including harassment, utility shutoffs, or physical removal — is prohibited.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; mandatory reinstatement of tenant
exceptions: Court-ordered evictions following proper legal process

quiz.q: What type of eviction is legal in Lebanon?
options: Eviction after non-payment of rent for 2 months
Court-ordered evictions following proper legal process
quiz.explanation: Only court-ordered evictions following proper legal procedures are lawful in Lebanon. Self-help evictions are prohibited and criminal.

laws.title: Illegal Airspace Violations
laws.subtitle: Flying unauthorized aircraft in Lebanese airspace
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon airspace is regulated by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. Operating unauthorized aircraft — including drones above specified weight thresholds and altitudes — in Lebanese airspace without clearance is illegal and can have serious security implications given regional tensions.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; aircraft confiscation
exceptions: Authorized commercial aviation under international agreements
Military aircraft under proper authorization

quiz.q: Which body regulates Lebanon airspace?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon Directorate General of Civil Aviation regulates national airspace and authorizes aircraft operations.

laws.title: Unauthorized Access to Government Databases
laws.subtitle: Hacking into official government systems
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon Cybercrime Law prohibits unauthorized access to government information systems, including databases containing personal, financial, or security information. Given Lebanon governance challenges, protecting official data systems is a priority.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; enhanced if data is extracted or damaged
exceptions: Authorized security testing by official IT teams

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for hacking into government databases and extracting data?
quiz.explanation: Unauthorized access to government databases carries up to 5 years imprisonment in Lebanon, with enhancement possible if data is extracted.

laws.title: Bribery of Judges
laws.subtitle: Paying or receiving bribes in the judicial system
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits bribery of judges and other judicial officials. Both the person offering a bribe and the judge accepting it commit serious criminal offenses. Judicial corruption undermines the rule of law and denies citizens fair justice.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; permanent removal from judicial position
exceptions: None — judicial bribery is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Corruption of Justice

quiz.q: What happens to a judge convicted of accepting bribes in Lebanon?
options: Hard labor and permanent removal from position
quiz.explanation: Judges convicted of accepting bribes in Lebanon face hard labor imprisonment and permanent removal from the judicial position.

laws.title: Social Security Fraud
laws.subtitle: Making false claims to obtain social security benefits
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon social security system provides benefits for employment-related injuries, illness, and family allowances. Making false claims to obtain benefits — including faking injuries, misrepresenting employment status, or claiming for non-existent dependents — is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; repayment of fraudulently obtained benefits
exceptions: Good-faith mistakes in benefit claims promptly corrected

quiz.q: What types of benefits does Lebanon social security system provide?
options: Employment injury, illness, and family allowances
quiz.explanation: Lebanon National Social Security Fund provides benefits for employment injuries, illness, and family allowances to covered workers.

laws.title: Forced Displacement of Civilians
laws.subtitle: Compelling people to flee their homes through threats
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law and international humanitarian law both prohibit the forced displacement of civilian populations. Given Lebanon history of sectarian conflict and refugee crises, laws against deliberately causing civilian displacement are particularly significant.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years
exceptions: None — forced displacement is always criminal under domestic and international law
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — International Humanitarian Law

quiz.q: Why is forced displacement law particularly significant in Lebanon history?
options: Lebanon has always had perfect sectarian harmony
Lebanon history of sectarian conflict and refugee crises makes it very relevant
Lebanon is a major refugee-hosting country only
The law was recently introduced after civil war
quiz.explanation: Lebanon history of civil war, sectarian conflict, and refugee movements makes laws against forced displacement of civilians especially significant.

laws.title: Broadcasting Without License
laws.subtitle: Operating unlicensed television or radio stations
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law requires radio and television broadcasters to obtain licenses from the National Council for Audiovisual Media. Operating broadcasting without a license, or after license revocation, is a criminal offense. Lebanon has a notably pluralistic and vibrant media landscape.
laws.penalty: Fine; equipment confiscation; up to 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: Community radio operating within approved community broadcasting frameworks

quiz.q: Which body issues broadcasting licenses in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon National Council for Audiovisual Media regulates and issues licenses for television and radio broadcasting.

laws.title: Attempted Murder
laws.subtitle: Taking actions with intent to kill that do not result in death
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law punishes attempted murder — taking actions with the specific intent to kill another person that do not result in death — with serious penalties approaching those for completed murder. The criminal intent is judged as severely as the completed act.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years; enhanced if premeditated
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense that goes further than intended

quiz.q: How does Lebanese law treat attempted murder compared to completed murder?
options: With penalties approaching those for completed murder
With identical penalties to completed murder
quiz.explanation: Lebanese law imposes serious penalties for attempted murder — approaching but not identical to those for completed murder — recognizing the criminal intent.

laws.title: Prison Break and Assistance to Escape
laws.subtitle: Escaping from lawful custody or helping prisoners escape
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law criminalizes escaping from lawful custody, as well as helping prisoners or detainees to escape. This applies to jails, prisons, and any other form of official detention. Given Lebanon prison conditions, escape attempts have been documented.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment for escape; up to 5 years for assisting escape
exceptions: None for intentional escape or assistance
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Against the Administration of Justice

quiz.q: Does helping a prisoner escape carry the same penalty as the escape itself in Lebanon?
options: Greater penalty than the escape itself
quiz.explanation: Assisting a prisoner to escape carries a greater penalty (up to 5 years) than the escape itself (up to 3 years) in Lebanon.

laws.title: Adulteration of Food and Drink
laws.subtitle: Adding harmful substances to food or beverages
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese food safety law prohibits adulterating food and beverages with harmful substances, or misrepresenting the content and origin of food products. This includes adding prohibited substances, mislabeling, or substituting inferior ingredients without disclosure.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; business closure
exceptions: Approved food additives used within permitted levels

quiz.q: What constitutes food adulteration under Lebanese law?
options: Adding harmful substances or misrepresenting food content
Selling food past its best-before date
quiz.explanation: Food adulteration in Lebanon includes adding harmful substances and misrepresenting the true content, origin, or quality of food products.

laws.title: Kidnapping of Foreign Nationals
laws.subtitle: Abducting foreigners on Lebanese soil
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon has experienced kidnappings of foreign nationals, particularly journalists, aid workers, and diplomats. Lebanese law treats the kidnapping of foreigners on Lebanese territory as a serious crime, and such cases often attract international attention and pressure.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 20 years; life imprisonment if victim killed
exceptions: None — kidnapping is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Crimes Against Foreigners

quiz.q: What categories of foreign nationals have historically been kidnapping targets in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Journalists, aid workers, and diplomats have historically been among the most targeted foreign nationals for kidnapping in Lebanon.

laws.title: Counterfeit Pharmaceutical Production
laws.subtitle: Manufacturing fake medicines
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits the production of counterfeit, substandard, or falsely labeled pharmaceutical products. Such medicines may be ineffective or actively harmful, endangering patient health. The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health enforces pharmaceutical quality standards.
laws.penalty: Hard labor; up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical manufacturers under full regulatory oversight

quiz.q: Which ministry enforces pharmaceutical quality standards in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health is responsible for enforcing pharmaceutical quality standards and combating counterfeit medicine production.

laws.title: Pyramid Scheme Operation
laws.subtitle: Running fraudulent investment pyramid schemes
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits pyramid and Ponzi schemes — investment arrangements that pay returns using new investor money rather than genuine profits. Such schemes inevitably collapse, causing widespread financial losses. Lebanon financial crisis environment has increased vulnerability.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: None — all pyramid schemes are illegal regardless of claimed legitimacy

quiz.q: How does Lebanon financial crisis context affect pyramid scheme vulnerability?
options: Desperate citizens seeking investment returns are more vulnerable to such schemes
Only wealthy people invest in schemes
The crisis ended all investment activity
quiz.explanation: Lebanon economic crisis has left many citizens desperate for investment returns, increasing their vulnerability to pyramid and Ponzi scheme operators.

laws.title: Ship Abandonment and Maritime Fraud
laws.subtitle: Abandoning cargo vessels or committing maritime insurance fraud
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese maritime law prohibits captains and ship owners from abandoning vessels with crew aboard, and prohibits maritime insurance fraud including deliberately sinking ships for insurance payouts. Beirut Port is a major regional hub, making maritime law compliance essential.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; enhanced if crew harmed
exceptions: Emergency vessel abandonment with proper evacuation of crew when vessel is unsalvageable

quiz.q: Why is Lebanese maritime law particularly important given Beirut role?
options: Lebanon has the largest navy in the region
Beirut Port is a major regional hub
Lebanon has the highest sailor population
quiz.explanation: Beirut Port role as a major regional shipping hub makes Lebanese maritime law compliance especially important for regional commerce.

laws.title: Faulty Construction
laws.subtitle: Building structures that violate safety codes
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese construction law requires buildings to meet structural safety, fire safety, and seismic resistance standards. Constructing buildings that violate these standards — through deliberate cost-cutting on materials, ignoring engineering requirements, or forging safety inspections — endangers lives.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if building collapses or people harmed
exceptions: Minor non-structural deviations disclosed and corrected

quiz.q: What natural hazard makes seismic resistance standards particularly important in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon is located in a seismically active region, making earthquake resistance standards essential in construction safety codes.

laws.title: Trafficking of Stolen Goods
laws.subtitle: Buying or selling property known to be stolen
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law prohibits trading in stolen property — knowingly buying, selling, or storing goods that have been stolen. Receiving stolen goods creates a market that incentivizes theft and other property crimes.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; forfeiture of stolen goods
exceptions: Good-faith purchase without knowledge of theft
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Receiving Stolen Property

quiz.q: What is required for criminal liability for trading in stolen goods in Lebanon?
options: Any purchase of goods below market price
Knowledge that the goods were stolen
quiz.explanation: Criminal liability for trading in stolen goods requires knowledge that the goods were stolen — good-faith purchase without such knowledge is not criminal.

laws.title: Medical Fraud and False Insurance Claims
laws.subtitle: Submitting false medical claims for insurance reimbursement
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits submitting false or inflated claims to insurance companies and the National Social Security Fund. Medical providers who bill for procedures not performed, or claim for more expensive treatments than provided, commit fraud against both insurers and the health system.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; professional license revocation
exceptions: Good-faith billing errors with prompt correction when identified
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Social Security Law — Fraud Provisions

quiz.q: What body is defrauded when doctors submit false social security medical claims?
quiz.explanation: False medical claims submitted to Lebanon social security system defraud the National Social Security Fund, ultimately harming all contributors.

laws.title: Unauthorized Telecommunications Operations
laws.subtitle: Operating communications infrastructure without licenses
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese telecommunications law requires all providers of telephone, internet, and other communication services to obtain licenses from the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority. Unauthorized telecommunications operations undermine spectrum management and consumer protection.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; equipment seizure
exceptions: Amateur radio operators within licensed frequency allocations

quiz.q: Which body issues telecommunications licenses in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon Telecommunications Regulatory Authority issues licenses and regulates all commercial telecommunications service providers.

laws.title: Cyber Attacks on Financial Institutions
laws.subtitle: Hacking or disrupting banks and financial services
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law imposes enhanced penalties for cyber attacks targeting banks, insurance companies, and other financial institutions. Given Lebanon banking crisis and the fragility of public trust in financial institutions, protecting them from cyber attacks is a national priority.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; up to 10 years if significant financial harm caused
exceptions: Authorized security testing by certified professionals under contract

quiz.q: Why is protecting financial institutions from cyber attacks particularly important in Lebanon?
options: Lebanese banks hold the most deposits in the world
Lebanon banking crisis makes public trust in banks especially fragile
Lebanon has the most advanced banking technology
quiz.explanation: Lebanon banking crisis has severely damaged public trust in financial institutions, making cyber attacks on banks especially damaging to an already fragile system.

laws.title: Espionage Using Electronic Means
laws.subtitle: Electronic surveillance or data theft for foreign intelligence
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law, reinforced by the 2018 Cybercrime Law, prohibits using electronic means to collect intelligence for foreign powers. This includes hacking, installing surveillance software, and intercepting electronic communications on behalf of foreign intelligence services.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 15 years
exceptions: Authorized bilateral intelligence cooperation under state-to-state agreements

quiz.q: What 2018 law reinforced Lebanon traditional espionage prohibitions?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon 2018 Cybercrime Law reinforced traditional espionage prohibitions by specifically addressing electronic surveillance and cyber espionage for foreign powers.

laws.title: Destruction of Cultural Heritage Sites
laws.subtitle: Damaging historical and archaeological monuments
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon extraordinary heritage — Phoenician ports, Roman ruins, Crusader castles — is protected by law. Deliberately damaging or destroying protected heritage sites is a serious criminal offense that deprives future generations of irreplaceable connections to the past.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; mandatory restoration costs
exceptions: Authorized conservation work that inadvertently affects adjacent structures

quiz.q: What ancient civilizations left heritage sites protected under Lebanese law?
options: Phoenician, Roman, and Crusader among others
quiz.explanation: Lebanon rich archaeological heritage includes Phoenician ports, Roman temples, Byzantine churches, and Crusader fortifications, all protected by heritage law.

laws.title: Dynamite Fishing
laws.subtitle: Using explosives to stun or kill fish
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon coastal fishing law prohibits the use of explosives for fishing. Dynamite fishing — throwing explosive charges into water to stun or kill fish — destroys coral reefs, kills non-target marine life, and devastates ecosystems. Despite prohibition, it has been practiced on Lebanon coast.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; confiscation of equipment
exceptions: None — explosive fishing is always destructive and prohibited

quiz.q: What collateral damage does dynamite fishing cause beyond the intended catch?
options: Coral reef destruction, killing of non-target species, and ecosystem damage
quiz.explanation: Dynamite fishing destroys coral reef ecosystems, kills indiscriminate species, and causes long-term damage to the marine environment beyond the intended catch.

laws.title: Bank Robbery
laws.subtitle: Robbing financial institutions using force or threats
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese criminal law treats armed robbery of banks and other financial institutions as a particularly serious violent crime. Given Lebanon banking crisis and the substantial cash holdings outside the formal banking system, robbery risks have increased.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 20 years; enhanced if weapons used or people harmed
exceptions: None — bank robbery is always a serious crime
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Penal Code — Robbery and Aggravated Theft

quiz.q: How has Lebanon banking crisis affected the context for bank robbery laws?
options: It reduced robbery risk by reducing bank holdings
Increased cash outside formal banking has raised robbery risks
Banks have closed eliminating the crime opportunity
Laws were relaxed during the crisis
quiz.explanation: Lebanon banking crisis has led to more cash circulating outside formal banking, increasing the context in which robbery laws operate.

laws.title: Workplace Safety Violations
laws.subtitle: Maintaining dangerous working conditions for employees
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese labor law requires employers to maintain safe working conditions meeting occupational health and safety standards. Exposing workers to preventable hazards — dangerous machinery, toxic substances, electrical hazards — without adequate protection constitutes a violation.
laws.penalty: Fine; suspension of operations; criminal charges if injuries result
exceptions: Inherently hazardous work with full risk disclosure, training, and protective equipment provided

quiz.q: What is required when workers must perform inherently hazardous work in Lebanon?
options: Full risk disclosure, training, and proper protective equipment
quiz.explanation: Workers in inherently hazardous roles in Lebanon must receive full risk disclosure, proper training, and adequate protective equipment.

laws.title: Illegal Sand Mining
laws.subtitle: Extracting sand from beaches and riverbeds without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese beaches and riverbeds have been damaged by illegal sand mining for construction. Sand extraction destroys coastal ecosystems, accelerates erosion, and depletes natural resources. Lebanese authorities have attempted to crack down on this widespread illegal activity.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 100 million LBP; up to 2 years imprisonment; mandatory site restoration
exceptions: Licensed industrial sand operations in designated areas with environmental assessment
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Environment Protection Act — Natural Resources

quiz.q: What ecological damage does illegal beach sand mining cause in Lebanon?
options: Coastal erosion, ecosystem destruction, and resource depletion
quiz.explanation: Illegal sand mining in Lebanon destroys coastal ecosystems, accelerates beach erosion, and depletes non-renewable natural sand resources.

laws.title: Trafficking of Women for Prostitution
laws.subtitle: Exploiting women through forced commercial sex work
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits trafficking women and girls for commercial sexual exploitation. While Lebanon has faced criticism for the artiste visa system that was abused for trafficking, the underlying criminal law prohibits forced prostitution and trafficking for sexual purposes.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 10 years; enhanced for organized networks
exceptions: None — all trafficking for sexual exploitation is criminal

quiz.q: What visa system was historically criticized for enabling trafficking in Lebanon?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon artiste visa system was historically criticized for being abused to traffic women for commercial sexual exploitation in nightclubs.

laws.title: False Advertising
laws.subtitle: Making misleading commercial claims to consumers
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese consumer protection law prohibits false or misleading advertising. This includes claims about product efficacy, pricing, origin, and quality that are deceptive. In the context of Lebanon economic crisis, misleading financial and investment advertising has been particularly harmful.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment; mandatory corrective advertising
exceptions: Recognized advertising puffery — exaggerated claims that no reasonable person would take literally
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Consumer Protection Act — Advertising Standards

quiz.q: What type of false advertising has been particularly harmful during Lebanon economic crisis?
quiz.explanation: Misleading investment and financial advertising has been particularly harmful during Lebanon crisis, exploiting desperate citizens seeking to protect savings.

laws.title: Unauthorized Research on Human Subjects
laws.subtitle: Conducting medical research without ethics approval
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese medical research ethics require that any clinical research involving human subjects obtain prior approval from an Institutional Review Board or ethics committee. Conducting research without such approval violates both ethical principles and legal requirements.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment if subjects harmed
exceptions: Emergency treatment of consenting patients with expedited ethics review
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Medical Professions Law — Research Ethics

quiz.q: What body must approve human subjects research in Lebanon?
options: Institutional Review Board or ethics committee
quiz.explanation: Human subjects research in Lebanon requires prior approval from an Institutional Review Board or ethics committee to protect participant rights.

laws.title: Smuggling Refugees
laws.subtitle: Organizing illegal border crossings for desperate migrants
laws.fullDescription: Lebanon, as a country hosting large refugee populations from Syria and Palestine, is both affected by and implicated in migration crimes. Organized smuggling of refugees across borders for profit — whether into Lebanon or through it to Europe — is criminalized.
laws.penalty: Hard labor for up to 7 years; enhanced for organized networks
exceptions: Humanitarian assistance to refugees not motivated by financial gain

quiz.q: What large refugee population does Lebanon host that makes migration law particularly relevant?
quiz.explanation: Lebanon hosts large Palestinian and Syrian refugee populations, making migration law especially relevant in the Lebanese context.

laws.title: Telecommunication Fraud
laws.subtitle: Using phone or internet services fraudulently
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law prohibits telecommunication fraud including SIM card cloning, making calls using others accounts, and operating unauthorized international calling services that bypass Ogero telecom infrastructure. Telecom fraud harms both consumers and state revenues.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized voice-over-IP services under proper telecommunications licensing

quiz.q: What does SIM card cloning allow fraudsters to do?
options: Use another person phone number to make calls at their expense
quiz.explanation: SIM card cloning allows fraudsters to replicate a victim phone number and make calls or use services at the victim expense.

laws.title: Drone Surveillance Without Authorization
laws.subtitle: Using drones to spy on individuals or restricted areas
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law, reinforced by the 2018 Cybercrime Law and aviation regulations, prohibits using drones to conduct unauthorized surveillance of individuals, military installations, or other restricted areas. The regional security context makes unauthorized drone flights particularly sensitive.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; drone confiscation
exceptions: Authorized journalism and filming with prior permissions
Official state surveillance under judicial authorization
laws.sourceLabel: Lebanese Aviation Law and Cybercrime Law — Drone Regulations

quiz.q: Why is unauthorized drone use particularly sensitive in Lebanon?
options: Regional security tensions make airspace violations especially serious
quiz.explanation: Regional security tensions in Lebanon and its neighborhood make unauthorized drone flights near military installations particularly serious security concerns.

laws.title: Illegal Hunting
laws.subtitle: Hunting protected species or during closed seasons
laws.fullDescription: Lebanese law restricts hunting to permitted species during designated seasons.
